answer: accumulated signal across many panels. Fresh sybil identities enter panels together, but their mutual positive votes are diluted because each epoch re-sorts jurors, so a forged identity behaves like a noisy plume that disperses rather than a durable voting bloc; only identities that consistently earn approval from strangers gain real economic weight. An attacker therefore pays for every duplicate identity (key management, staking collateral, and per-epoch activity fees) while its expected payoff stays near zero, since collusion requires surviving many independent random draws.
